text:
The Rangers' goaltending has been the story of their week without anyone pulling a goalie. James Reimer went on unconditional waivers on Nov. 7 to have his contract terminated, Dylan Garand has taken 13 of 19 starts, and tonight in Calgary it's Joonas Korpisalo's turn, in his second start of the season after he won his debut in Seattle on Saturday. One start is nothing to judge, but a team that's trimmed its depth chart is going to find out quickly whether its backup can carry a few nights.

New York arrives annoyed, probably. Monday in Edmonton the Rangers took 65% of the expected goals (the quality of their chances) and lost 3-1, mostly because Devon Levi saved 2.6 goals more than the shots deserved. They've won the chance battle in four of their last five. J.T. Miller is part of the frustration: no goals in five games on 3.0 expected goals, the kind of drought that usually ends on its own. Alexis Lafrenière, whose alley-oop goal on Saturday was his seventh (ESPN had it as the league lead at the time), keeps driving the top line with Mika Zibanejad and Gabe Perreault.

Calgary's crease has a story too. Devin Cooley has pushed his way to the front: .945 and 7.0 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, all wins, while Dustin Wolf had a rough night against the Ducks. That's carrying a team that has been outplayed more often than not, with 43% of the expected goals over its last five and a winning chance battle only once. Sunday's overtime win over Philadelphia, on Matt Coronato's goal, is the template: hang around, let Cooley steal time, find one.

There are side plots for the home crowd. Coronato is one goal from 50 for his career, Jake Middleton plays his 400th game, and Brennan Othmann and Ryan Strome both get a look at the team that moved them. Our numbers lean New York, 3.06 expected goals to 2.77, and give the Rangers a coin flip's worth of playoff odds (53%) against Calgary's 11%.
headline: Korpisalo gets the call as the Rangers' crease gets crowded

hunch.text: Our numbers like the Rangers, but our gut says a goalie on a heater beats a backup making his second start of the year. Calgary steals one again.
